decisions.reason: As a finish and design extension of the firm’s core drainage range, it fits existing manufacturing and market knowledge well, so absorptive capacity is high and the line is likely to be retained despite some style-related demand uncertainty.

This shower channel is very close to the firm’s established technical and customer base, and its dedicated web presentation suggests enough strategic commitment to keep refining and selling it rather than withdraw it quickly.

Although the pump-assisted solution is somewhat more complex and may require more learning in installation and support, it still builds on the firm’s drainage know-how and in-house R&D, making continuation more likely than exit.

A tileable floor drain with grating is strongly aligned with the firm’s existing capabilities, barrier-free bathroom trend, and installer/planner relationships, so the firm would likely keep it on the market.
This stainless steel design grate is a close adjacent product that leverages the firm’s design-engineering strengths and broad portfolio logic, so there is little reason to remove it within a year.
